name: Charlotte Barker
life: “I used to work knots in the dark to keep the light out of a sleeping bunk.” Monday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Charlotte knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I took the seam apart strand by strand after my hands stopped tolerating heavy rope. It is still boat work.
appearance: Charlotte has a long silver braid, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Charlotte turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Charlotte thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Charlotte sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To salvage enough good cord to repair one more bag.
family: Ines Baldwin is Charlotte’s younger relative by marriage. Charlotte checks the date twice. Ines brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The almost scholarship*, Ines says, “I won the tuition and haven't dared tell my little sister that going means leaving her school runs to somebody else.”
connections: Ian Palmer. Untwisting the seam provides the cord for six little practice sails.

reactions.situation: Two makers want the same piece of sail
reactions.response: Charlotte lays both paper patterns on the piece before anybody cuts.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Charlotte asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.

reactions.situation: When family demands an immediate answer
reactions.response: Charlotte asks them to walk to the corner together and listen until the corner comes.
